title: Nakayama: a finite module with IM=M is killed by an element of 1+I
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal and $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $IM=M$. Then there is $f\in R$ with $f-1\in I$ and $fM=0$ (that is, $fm=0$ for every $m\in M$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), item (1) (item-nakayama): 'If IM = M and M is finite, then there exists an f in 1 + I such that fM = 0'
